name: Service Worker offline caching
plain: Installs a script that caches pages and answers requests when offline.
meaning: A site can keep running its own code between visits and serve content from a local cache. Safari deletes script-written storage after 7 days without interaction; Chrome keeps it until cleared.

access.persistence: Persists until unregistered or storage cleared; Safari ITP may delete after 7 days of no interaction
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Same origin only; scope limited to script path unless Service-Worker-Allowed header is set
steps: fetch events return cached or network responses

limits.headline: Can save pages on your device so the site works offline
limits.user_action: You open the site once. It installs by itself, with no pop up.
can: Save pages, images and files on your device for later
Show saved pages when you have no signal
Answer or change requests the site makes, even when you are offline
cannot: Work on a site that has not been opened over a secure connection (HTTPS)
Use unlimited storage; browsers set a limit and may clear it
Stay saved forever; Safari on iPhone can clear it after 7 days of no use
limits.reach_label: Stays on your device between visits
limits.differs: Safari on iPhone can clear saved data after about 7 days without a visit, unless the site is added to your Home Screen.

story.what_it_is: A site can install a helper that stores pages and works when you are offline.

marketing.name: Service workers
marketing.pitch: web.dev teaches service workers as the base of installable, offline capable web apps.

story.for_you: A site opens instantly the second time and may even work on a plane. You never approve it, and it lives on after you close the tab.
story.for_makers: Makers get offline use, quick starts and push messages, which lifts return visits. It also lets them update an app silently in the background.

use_cases.example: A music or podcast web app plays saved episodes with no signal.
A flight status or map site loads from its saved copy in an airport with weak wifi.
A lite social site opens in a flash on a slow phone.
A browser game stores its art and levels so it starts fast and plays offline.
A store saves its catalog shell so browsing is fast on a bad connection.
A malicious site may keep a helper installed to serve ads or show alerts later, which is why you can clear site data.

technical_bounds: Idle service workers terminate after about 30 s; a single event can run up to about 5 minutes in Chrome
Browser checks for a new worker script at most every 24 h (byte compare) and on navigation
Safari (ITP) caps script-writable storage including service worker registrations and Cache API at 7 days of no user interaction (not for Home Screen web apps)
Cache API quota shared with origin quota (Chrome up to 60% of disk per origin; Firefox about 10% of disk, up to 10 GiB per group)
Cannot run while the browser is closed except via push or background sync (permission and platform needed)

abuse: Persistent foothold for tracking and malware

history.change: ITP caps script-writable storage including SW at 7 days
